feed.title: Media, Design & Files — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Animista
entry.summary: A library of ready CSS animations you can play, tweak and copy the code from.

entry.title: Awesome Ant Design
entry.summary: A resource list for Ant Design, the enterprise-class UI design language.

entry.title: Awesome Creative Coding
entry.summary: A resource list for creative coding — programming to express rather than to function.

entry.title: Awesome Design Principles
entry.summary: A list of design principles for better, more consistent designs.

entry.title: Awesome Design Systems
entry.summary: A list of reusable component systems (design systems) guided by rules.

entry.title: Awesome FFmpeg
entry.summary: A resource list for FFmpeg, recording, converting and streaming audio/video.

entry.title: Awesome GIF
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for the GIF animated-image format. Unlike general image lists, it gathers only tools for creating, optimising and playing GIFs.

entry.title: Awesome Icons
entry.summary: A list of downloadable SVG/PNG/font icon projects. Unlike a single icon set, it lays dozens of sets side by side so you can pick by style and licence.

entry.title: Awesome Pixel Art
entry.summary: A list of tools and resources for pixel-level digital art. Unlike general drawing lists, it focuses on pixel editors, palettes and pixel-art tutorials.

entry.title: Awesome Product Design
entry.summary: A resource list covering the design process from concept to product. Unlike UI-kit lists it is process-focused: research, prototyping, usability testing and handoff.

entry.title: Awesome VLC
entry.summary: A list of plugins and resources for VLC, the cross-platform media player.

entry.title: Awesome Web Design
entry.summary: A web-design resource list for digital designers. Unlike developer lists it is aimed at designers: inspiration, typography, colour and design tools.

entry.title: Behance
entry.summary: Adobe's portfolio platform presenting full project case studies rather than single shots.

entry.title: Checklist Design
entry.summary: Actionable UI/UX checklists organised per component and per page.

entry.title: Color Hunt
entry.summary: A catalogue of ready-to-use colour palettes curated by community votes.

entry.title: Colorful
entry.summary: A resource list to help choose your next colour scheme. Unlike a single palette generator such as Coolors, it gathers generators, palettes and colour-theory resources together.

entry.title: Colormind
entry.summary: An AI generator that learns from photos and art to suggest harmonious colour palettes.

entry.title: cubic-bezier.com
entry.summary: A tool to craft CSS easing curves by hand and compare them against presets live.

entry.title: Dribbble
entry.summary: An inspiration community where designers share shots of their work and the industry takes its pulse.

entry.title: Easings.net
entry.summary: Visualises common easing curves and lets you copy the cubic-bezier for each.

entry.title: Feather Icons
entry.summary: A simple, consistent open-source icon set at a single stroke weight. Unlike large libraries it offers a minimal visual language and small file size.

entry.title: Flaticon
entry.summary: A vast icon bank offering millions of vector icons in various styles.

entry.title: Font Awesome
entry.summary: The de facto icon and logo library of the web. Unlike collecting SVGs one by one you add icons as a font/CSS class in a single line.

entry.title: Fontsource
entry.summary: Lets you self-host open-source fonts via npm, with no external CDN needed.

entry.title: FreeImages
entry.summary: A free stock-photo archive whose roots go back to the old stock.xchng (SXC) community. Unlike Unsplash it is an older, broader archive; the trade-off is that image quality and licence terms vary from item to item.

entry.title: Freepik Stories
entry.summary: Freepik’s set of free, editable illustrations (Storyset); you can recolour them and download them animated. Unlike Freepik’s main archive, every image is customisable in the browser; free use requires attribution.

entry.title: GIMP
entry.summary: A full-featured image editor that is the open-source alternative to Photoshop. Unlike paid tools it is free and extensible with plugins.

entry.title: Gratisography
entry.summary: Unusual and creative free stock photos. Unlike archives such as Unsplash, its quirky, humorous shots steer clear of the clichéd stock-photo look.

entry.title: Haikei
entry.summary: A browser tool that generates blobs, waves and layered SVG background shapes.

entry.title: Hero Patterns
entry.summary: Repeatable SVG background patterns whose colour and opacity you tune, then copy the CSS.

entry.title: Humaaans
entry.summary: A library of human illustrations whose parts you can mix and pose. Unlike ready illustrations you assemble the figure limb by limb into an original scene.

entry.title: IcoFont
entry.summary: 2,100+ free icons to spice up designs, also usable as an icon font. Unlike downloading SVGs one by one, you drop an icon into a page with a CSS class.

entry.title: Iconfinder
entry.summary: A search engine hosting millions of icons and illustrations. Unlike a single icon set, you search across many designers’ sets at once; free and paid icons are mixed, so check the licence.

entry.title: Iconify
entry.summary: A library unifying 100+ icon sets under one API/component. Unlike installing each set separately you pull and mix them all from one interface.

entry.title: iconmonstr
entry.summary: A site with 316 free icon collections, all by a single designer. Unlike marketplaces such as Iconfinder it keeps one consistent style, so icons from different collections still sit well together.

entry.title: Icons8
entry.summary: A broad asset source offering icons, illustrations, photos and music in various styles. Unlike single-type sites it gives many types in one consistent visual language.

entry.title: Iconscout
entry.summary: A large collection bringing together icons, illustrations and 3D assets.

entry.title: IRA Design
entry.summary: Free illustrations with editable colours and objects. Unlike ready-made stock illustrations, you choose the gradient and objects to compose your own scene.

entry.title: LineIcons
entry.summary: An icon set of 2,000+ icons in a line style, part of it paid. Unlike mixed-style sets, every icon shares the same stroke weight and style.

entry.title: Lorem Picsum
entry.summary: A service returning placeholder photos at any size (the lorem ipsum of images). Unlike fixed placeholders you pass a size in the URL and get a real photo.
